Bahnar

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Bahnaric *rɔːj, from Proto-Mon-Khmer *ruj ~ *ruuj ~ *ruəj ~ *ruhaj (“fly (insect)”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /rɔːj/

Noun

[edit]

roi

  1. fly

Bourguignon

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Late Latin rex.

Noun

[edit]

roi m (plural rois, feminine roine)

  1. king

French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • roy (archaic, pre-1800)
  • roé (Quebec, eye dialect)

Etymology

[edit]

    Inherited from Middle French roy, from Old French roi, rei, from Latin rēgem.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ʁwa/, /χwa/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)
    • Homophones: Roy, rois, roua, rouas, rouât
    • Rhymes: -a
    • Hyphenation: roi

    Noun

    [edit]

    roi m (plural rois, feminine reine)

    1. king
      Le roi est mort.
      The king is dead.
    2. (chess) king
    3. (card games) king

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • au royaume des aveugles, les borgnes sont rois
    • être plus royaliste que le roi
    • fête des Rois
    • Filles du Roi
    • fou du roi
    • galette des rois
    • procureur du roi
    • roi des animaux
    • roi des cailles
    • roi des oiseaux
    • roi fainéant
    • roi mage
    • royaume
    • Vallée des rois

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • régalien
    • reine
    • royal
    • royaume
    • royauté

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • Antillean Creole: wa
    • Guianese Creole: rwè
    • Haitian Creole: wa
      • (perhaps) ⇒ Haitian Creole: lwa, lalwa
        • → English: loa
    • Karipúna Creole French: hué
    • Louisiana Creole: rwa
    • Seychellois Creole: lerwa
    • → Turkish: rua

    See also

    [edit]
    Chess pieces in French · pièces d'échecs (layout · text)
    roi dame tour fou cavalier pion
    Playing cards in French · cartes à jouer (layout · text)
    as deux trois quatre cinq six sept
    huit neuf dix valet dame roi joker

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “roi”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

    Indonesian

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Dutch rooi (“line”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈroi̯/ [ˈroi̯]
    • Rhymes: -oi̯
    • Syllabification: roi

    Noun

    [edit]

    roi

    1. (architecture, construction) building alignment

    Compounds

    [edit]
    • garis roi

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • roilen

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “roi”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

    Old French

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • rex (9th century)
    • rei
    • rai (Le Roman de Tristan, Thomas d'Angleterre)
    • roy

    Etymology

    [edit]

      From Latin rēgem.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (archaic) IPA(key): /ˈrei̯/
      • (classical) IPA(key): /ˈroi̯/, (northern) /ˈrei̯/
      • (late) IPA(key): /ˈro̯ɛ/, (northern) /ˈrɛ/

      Noun

      [edit]

      roi oblique singular, m (oblique plural rois, nominative singular rois, nominative plural roi)

      1. king
      2. (chess) king

      Related terms

      [edit]
      • roial
      • reaume

      Descendants

      [edit]
      • Middle French: roy
        • French: roi, roy (archaic, pre-1800), roé (Quebec, eye dialect)
          • Antillean Creole: wa
          • Guianese Creole: rwè
          • Haitian Creole: wa
            • (perhaps) ⇒ Haitian Creole: lwa, lalwa
              • → English: loa
          • Karipúna Creole French: hué
          • Louisiana Creole: rwa
          • Seychellois Creole: lerwa
          • → Turkish: rua
      • Norman:
        Continental Normandy: rei
        Guernsey: ré, roué
        Jersey: rouai
        Sark: rwe
      • Walloon: roy, rwè
      • → Middle English: roy, roye
        • English: roy

      Romanian

      [edit]

      Etymology

      [edit]

      Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic рои (roi), from Proto-Slavic *rojь. Compare Czech roj, Slovak roj and Serbo-Croatian roj.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • Rhymes: -oj

      Noun

      [edit]

      roi n (plural roiuri)

      1. swarm

      Declension

      [edit]
      singular plural
      indefinite definite indefinite definite
      nominative-accusative roi roiul roiuri roiurile
      genitive-dative roi roiului roiuri roiurilor
      vocative roiule roiurilor

      Vietnamese

      [edit]

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (Hà Nội) IPA(key): [zɔj˧˧]
      • (Huế) IPA(key): [ʐɔj˧˧]
      • (Saigon) IPA(key): [ɹɔj˧˧]

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

      From Proto-Vietic *p-rɔːj. Cognate with Chut [Rục] brɔːj¹, Kha Phong urɔːj.

      Noun

      [edit]

      (classifier cây, cái) roi • (鞕, 𩍢)

      1. whip, rod
      2. (zoology) flagellum
      Derived terms
      [edit]
      • trùng roi

      Etymology 2

      [edit]

      (This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.)

      Noun

      [edit]

      (classifier cây, trái, quả) roi

      1. (Northern Vietnam) wax apple (Syzygium samarangense)
        Synonym: mận
